answer: Each agent must lock a scarce deposit before it can submit work, and a randomly chosen peer checks the result before rewards are released. If the work is fraudulent or the agent disappears, the deposit is forfeited; honest agents recover it. A fake operator can create many identities, but must fund each one separately and risks losing every deposit caught cheating. The cedar, dawn, and onyx tasks still pay only once per accepted result, so splitting one operator into sybils raises exposure without multiplying rewards.
